correctness.rationale: In Z[[q]], the two series differ by E(q)^(-1) times Delta=E(q)^(p^(2a))-E(q^(p^a))^(p^a). Frobenius plus power lifting shows Delta is 0 modulo p^(a+1) as an entire series. For every 0<=j<a, lifting at exponent p^j shows all positive degrees below p^j vanish modulo p^(2a-j+1), with coefficient at p^j congruent to -p^(2a-j), and the second summand has no positive degree below p^a. Multiplication by the unit E(q)^(-1) preserves this first nonzero degree and leading residue. For r>=2a+1 the x-linear difference -p^(2a) ensures first failure at 1. Covers p=2, a=1, all r; exact finite arithmetic verifies multiple finite cases but is not used to infer infinity.

value.rationale: This directly resolves the stronger-prime-power-lifting gap prompted by Sharma 2026 and provides a natural complete classification: the exact maximal uniform modulus and the first failure index for every p-adic exponent r, with exact leading residues for all intermediate scales. The infinitely many prime-power parameters and all modulus exponents form a canonical arithmetic family, not an arbitrary finite slice. Its conceptual object is the congruence filtration between the Nekrasov--Okounkov and t-core series; the known prime-case and p^a-level congruences neither give this optimal classification nor the staircase. Proof simplicity and finite reproducibility are not the sole value arguments.
